records.question: How long does Spotify hold on to my personal information?
records.text:
Spotify keeps personal data only as long as it is necessary to provide the Spotify Service and for Spotify's legitimate and essential business purposes, such as maintaining service performance, making data-driven business decisions, complying with legal obligations, and resolving disputes [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

Specific retention periods include:
*   Data input as part of search queries is deleted after 90 days, subject to other applicable retention rules [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   Some data, like your Spotify username and profile information, is kept until your Spotify account is deleted [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   Streaming history is kept for the life of an account to support personalized recommendations and retrospective playlists [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

Users have the right to request the deletion of certain personal data, and some data can be deleted directly from the Spotify Service, such as a profile picture [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

records.question: Will Spotify give my money back if I cancel partway through a subscription period?
records.text: Generally, Spotify does not provide refunds or credits for any partial subscription periods, unless it is expressly stated in the Terms [Spotify – Billing and cancellation]. However, if Spotify permanently discontinues a Paid Subscription for which you prepaid fees before the end of your Prepaid Period, Spotify will refund the prorated portion of those prepaid fees after the discontinuation, provided your account and billing information are up to date [Spotify – Service limitations and modifications].

records.question: Can I team up with other Spotify customers to sue the company as a group?
records.text: No, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, both you and Spotify agree that claims brought against the other must be in an individual capacity, and neither party can participate as a plaintiff, claimant, or class member in any class, collective, consolidated, private attorney general, or representative proceeding [Spotify – Governing law, jurisdiction, class action waiver, and jury trial waiver].

records.question: How long does Netflix hang on to my details?

The duration of retention depends on factors such as your relationship with Netflix, the type of personal information, legal obligations, and the need to defend or resolve legal claims [Netflix – Retention of Personal Information].

records.question: Can other people read my Zoom Email messages?
records.text:
Zoom Email is end-to-end encrypted by default for emails sent and received directly between active Zoom Email users [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?]. When an email is end-to-end encrypted, only the users, and potentially account owners or designated account administrators depending on their settings, control the encryption key and thus have access to the email content, including the body text, subject line, attachments, and custom labels [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?].

However, if you share encrypted content, such as forwarding an encrypted Zoom Email to a third-party recipient without a Zoom Email account, the shared or forwarded content will not be end-to-end encrypted by Zoom [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?].

Zoom does have access to email metadata for basic email delivery, which includes the time, mimeID, and the number and size of attachments, as well as the email addresses in the from, to, cc, and bcc fields [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?].

Account owners, depending on their settings and designated account administrators, can access email content sent to and from users on their Zoom Email or Zoom Calendar accounts, even if those Zoom Emails are encrypted [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?].
cited_labels: [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?]

records.question: Can a teenager sign up for their own PayPal account?
records.text: To open a PayPal account, if you are an individual, you must be at least 18 years old [Paypal – Opening an account]. Additionally, if you are an individual, you must be at least 18 years old and have full legal capacity to enter into a contract to open and use a PayPal account [Paypal – Welcome to PayPal!].

records.question: How long does PayPal keep my information once I stop being a customer?
records.text:
When the relationship with PayPal ends, Personal Information used for that relationship is stored for the duration of the relationship plus 10 years, or for a period required by applicable local law, unless it needs to be kept longer as permitted by applicable law, such as for legal obligations, bankruptcy laws, AML obligations, litigation, investigations, audit, or compliance practices [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information].

Even if you close your account or request the deletion of Personal Information, PayPal may still need to keep some of it to comply with laws and other legal or governmental requirements, complete transactions, provide requested goods or services, detect and prevent illegal or fraudulent activity, or protect legal rights [Paypal – Your rights].

Additionally, after closing your account, PayPal may retain your electronic money for a time it reasonably requires to protect itself and/or any third party against risks like reversals, fees, fines, penalties, and other liabilities [Paypal – Closing Your PayPal Account].
cited_labels: [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information]

records.question: If I close my Strava account, does my data actually go away?

However, it may take up to 45 days for your personal information and system logs to be deleted from their systems [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data] [Strava – Retention of Information]. Additionally, Strava may keep some information to comply with the law or take other actions permitted by law [Strava – Deleting Information and Accounts and Downloading Your Data] [Strava – Retention of Information].
